text: Worked example eight point one. Bromomethane is a methyl halide, so S N two, with rate equals k times both concentrations. k is two times ten to the minus four over zero point one times zero point one: two times ten to the minus two. Doubling hydroxide doubles the rate, to four times ten to the minus four. But for the tertiary halide, the mechanism is S N one, hydroxide is not in the rate law, and doubling it changes nothing.
